details.gate_check: PASS with one reservation, reported honestly. Not a REQ restatement: REQ-TEST-REGISTRY says nothing about key vocabulary or repetition. Not a mechanism description: the truth-condition is the severity/outcome (error, non-PASS), not the parser's steps. Decidable: feed a declaration with an unadmitted key, read severity and the resulting check value. No test-presupposing wording, no implementation present-tense promotion (it does not say "the scanner emits"). Compound risk: two diagnostic codes appear. I judge this one predicate — "a key the field contract does not admit" — with two instances, matching §5.4's own grouping, not a conjunction of two obligations. A stricter reading would split it into two VOs.
details.mechanism: 詳細設計 §4.2 fixes the `rust-cargo` key vocabulary and the repeatable set (`case`/`related`, plus `target` for integration kinds per 別紙A §14.3); §4.4 routes annotation syntax violations to the §5.4 diagnostic codes; §5.4 assigns both codes severity `error`, and error severity drives the affected entity's check items non-PASS. Detection sits adapter-side, so it does not breach VO-REGISTRY-05 (core never interprets declaration syntax); core classifies the returned diagnostic. The distinct-spelling branch of E-SCAN-005 is separately owned by core at resolution time (§6.1.1) and is already claimed by VO-REGISTRY-11.
details.req_anchor: Existing REQ suffices; no new REQ needed. REQ-TEST-REGISTRY (.verify/req/REQ-TEST-REGISTRY.yaml → SPEC-REQDEF §7,§8,§9,§10,§32-3) anchors it: 要件定義 §7.1 defines 構造上完全 as materializing a 構文上有効な Test ID and required metadata from the source declaration, which a duplicated non-repeatable key defeats. REQ-P-002 (Fail Closed) anchors the error-not-warning choice. The unknown-key obligation has no sentence of its own in 要件定義; it enters legitimately through 基本仕様 §16's explicit delegation of 宣言構文とパースエラーの扱い to 詳細設計本冊.
details.rationale: The citation pointed at §5.4, but the operative grammar rule lives in §4.2; both are 詳細設計本冊, which is normative, and 基本仕様 §16 expressly delegates this topic there — so the obligation is spec-imposed, not merely implied by the test. Its normative content is substantive: unknown `@vtest.*` keys are errors "警告ではなく" because a typo must not silently become a no-op. 別紙C carries acceptance criteria only for the target-alias branch of E-SCAN-005, so annex coverage does not absorb it. No frozen VO claims the field-contract predicate; the gap is real and the amendment is warranted rather than manufactured.

details.rationale: The suspicion's pointer (VO-PARALLEL-09 presupposes atomic publication) does not survive reading §16.1. That section is titled 「ロック不要の根拠」 and its non-collision claim is scoped to ULID filenames; the pure-read sentence governs the reader's basis. The spec does address the torn/malformed-file case — reader-side and fail-closed: E-SCAN-001 (parse failure → DiscoveryBatch Incomplete), E-SCAN-010 (id/filename/schema mismatch → record excluded from valid results, never PASS). A partially visible record is therefore already dispositioned by normative text without any writer-atomicity obligation. Atomic publication is a sound implementation choice, not a spec contract.
details.mechanism: Implementation-level only: crates/vtest-store/src/records.rs::write_new_record writes to a ULID-suffixed .tmp, publishes via fs::hard_link (fails on collision, preserving prior content), then unlinks the temp — best-effort, so a crash can leave residue. write_atomic is the entity-file counterpart. No normative document names, requires, or constrains this mechanism; 基本仕様 §15 item 15 delegates 「並列編集時の物理的保存方式」 to §5.2, which specifies only file-per-record/ULID/immutability. The mechanism therefore discharges no stated obligation — it is defense the spec never asked for.
details.req_anchor: No anchoring REQ exists. REQ-PARALLEL-DEV (要件定義 §29) enumerates seven concrete demands — no shared ledger, blast-radius containment, ID-collision detection, dangling-reference detection, semantic-conflict detection, rebuildable indexes, no memory-dependent sync — none of which is write atomicity, and it explicitly delegates 競合回避方式 to 基本設計, which then does not impose it. REQ-NFR-001 (並列変更に耐えられること) is discharged by 基本仕様 §13's mapping to §5.2. Creating a new REQ to host this would be inventing an upstream obligation to justify a downstream test; not warranted.

details.mechanism: The TestWireCodec capability defined in 詳細設計 本冊 §5.2: core holds only the neutral ExecutionDescriptor, and the rust-cargo codec exclusively owns the version-1 compat triple. On read, the codec discharges the obligation by preferring `execution`, cross-checking any coexisting compat set for equality of the derived coordinates, deriving a descriptor from the compat set only when it is complete and mutually consistent, and rejecting all other shapes fail-closed instead of synthesizing an empty selector or Rust default. Non-rust-cargo codecs never interpret the fields at all.
details.existing_vo_check: Dumped and read all 154 claims, not a keyword subset. No VO covers wire-input decode. VO-ADAPTER-12 is explicitly output-only ("are output only by the rust-cargo codec... no empty, dummy, or Rust-default values are ever generated") and says nothing about accepting/rejecting input. VO-ADAPTER-02 constrains the model shape (fields absent from TestEntity), not decode. VO-EXEC-12/13 and VO-ADAPTER-10 govern Evidence-record compat (adapter ID, hashes.target_fn, singular target_execution) — a different record and field family. VO-REGISTRY-04/08 and VO-STRUCTOP-11 govern the scan/Form path, not Test JSON. Genuinely absent.

proposed_vo.claim: A Test wire input yields an ExecutionDescriptor only when it carries `execution`, or carries a complete and mutually consistent Rust compatibility set (filter, package, test_target) that denotes the same execution coordinates as any coexisting `execution`; every other input is rejected rather than treated as executable, and no empty selector or default coordinate is synthesized.

details.gate_check: PASS. Not a REQ restatement — §27 states language neutrality; this states a decidable acceptance condition on one wire input. Not a mechanism description — it names a truth-condition evaluable by presenting inputs and observing accept/reject, with no reference to a call, type, or error variant. Not test-presupposing — no assertion, fixture, or "the test shows" wording; the codec's internal API names are deliberately absent. Not implementation-promoted — phrased as an obligation on any conforming reader, not as a present-tense description of current code. Single condition — one fail-closed only-when rule with its complement, mirroring the spec's own sentence, not two conjoined rejections. Decidable, no vague qualifiers.
details.rationale: The suspicion's pointer (基本仕様 122) lands on the output paragraph, which VO-ADAPTER-12 already discharges; the operative normative text is the next paragraph, line 126, and it is unambiguously must-strength. Four normative layers repeat it (基本仕様 §2.4, 本冊 §5.2, 別紙A §12.1, 別紙C §18.3.9); none of it is 別紙B-only or inference. So the obligation is real, is the input-side complement of VO-ADAPTER-12, and no frozen VO expresses it. Corroborating, the test's `@vtest.covers VO-ARUST-001` names an ID absent from the frozen 154 — the pointer predates the freeze. Recommend adding VO-ADAPTER-13 in freeze-v3; repo untouched.

normative_citations: 詳細設計 本冊 §11.2 Evidence 鮮度判定 (L1384): 「対象 Test の Evidence のうち**最新のもの**について：」 — the freshness algorithm operates on the latest Evidence.

詳細設計 本冊 §7.3 (L1010): 「**§11.2 が選択した最新 Evidence** の `evidence_validity` が PASS のとき…」 and (L1017) 「runtime 側は §11.2 が選択した**最新 Evidence だけ**を用いる…古い有効 Evidence へフォールバックしない」 — the selection is load-bearing for runtime proof.

詳細設計 本冊 §1.2 依存クレート表 (L70): 「| 日時 | `time` | **RFC 3339** |」 — record timestamps are RFC 3339, which admits non-Z offsets. No spec text anywhere restricts timestamps to UTC/Z (searched 時刻/タイムゾーン/オフセット/UTC across all docs: zero hits).
基本仕様 v0.1 §附録表 17 (L726): 「監査レコードは複数保持でき、**最新の有効レコードを判定に用いる**」 — same 最新-selection duty in the parent layer.
details.req_anchor: REQ-TEST-EXECUTION (要件定義 §15 Execution Evidence の鮮度: 「過去のPASSが現在のPASSへ無条件に引き継がれてはならない」). Existing anchor; no new REQ needed. §15 supplies the freshness duty, §11.2 supplies the selection duty this VO fixes.
details.mechanism: §11.2 requires the freshness algorithm to run against one designated record per Test. The only execution-time field in the §3.7 Evidence schema is `executed_at` (RFC 3339); ULID record IDs are declared (基本仕様 §5.2, L154) for parallel filename collision avoidance, not ordering. So the designation is discharged by comparing `executed_at` as normalized instants before the five freshness conditions are applied — a single Evidence per Test enters §11.2, with no fallback (§7.3 L1017).
details.existing_vo_check: Not covered. VO-STATAUDIT-10 and VO-EXEC-05/06 all say "the latest Evidence selected by §11.2" / "the Evidence" — they presuppose the selection and constrain only what happens after it. VO-SEMAUDIT-05 ("any FAIL yields FAIL, else the latest verdict") is audit records, not Evidence, and likewise leaves ordering undefined. VO-EXEC-04/11/13 constrain record contents. No VO in the frozen 154 states which of several Evidence records is the latest. Separately: the test declares `covers VO-VERIFY-001`, an ID absent from the frozen 154 — part of why this fired.

proposed_vo.claim: When a Test has more than one Evidence record, the record whose §11.2 freshness is judged is the one whose executed_at denotes the greatest chronological instant under RFC 3339 offset normalization, never the lexically greatest timestamp string.

details.gate_check: PASS. Not a REQ restatement: 要件定義 §15 is hash-binding freshness, this is selection ordering. Not a mechanism description: it states a truth-condition decidable from two records plus their timestamps. Decidable: offset-normalized instant comparison is total on RFC 3339 values. Single condition (the trailing "never lexical" is the contrapositive of the same condition, matching existing VO style, not a second obligation). No implementation promotion: `compare_evidence_recency` is not named. Not test-presupposing: worded independently of the test's @vtest.intent. Deliberately excluded as implementation policy, not spec-imposed: tie-breaking and unparseable-timestamp handling.
details.rationale: 最新 is a temporal superlative; its literal content is chronological recency. Since §1.2 fixes RFC 3339 and no spec text restricts timestamps to Z, lexical string order provably diverges from 最新 (09:00+09:00 sorts above 00:30Z yet is 30 min earlier), so "never lexical" is the contrapositive of the quoted obligation, not a new inference. Two derivation steps disclosed rather than upgraded: (a) the key is executed_at — argued from §3.7 being the only execution-time field and ULID's stated collision-avoidance purpose, not stated outright; (b) the RFC 3339 designation sits in the 依存クレート table, the weakest normative link in the chain. Neither candidate key licenses lexical ordering, so the core obligation is not two-readable.

詳細設計本冊 §1.2 主要依存クレート (L67): 「Rust source走査 | `ignore` | `vtest-adapter-rust`が所有する`.gitignore`準拠の走査」 — descriptive reinforcement only.
詳細設計別紙C §18.3.9 (L206): 「`vtest-scan`は…`*.rs`列挙…を所有しない」 — ownership of the walk (already covered by VO-REGISTRY-05 / VO-ADAPTER-09), not scope semantics.

details.req_anchor: No REQ imposes discovery-scope semantics. 要件定義 §7.1 defines the discovered set D as 「登録adapterがTestとして発見した実行可能なtest construct」 — scope-agnostic by construction; §23 and NFRs are silent on file walking. Nearest anchor is REQ-ADAPTER-BOUNDARY (the walk is adapter-owned, 別紙C §18.3.9), which carries ownership but not scope. Strictly, scope semantics ("VCS-ignored files are out of the verified population") has no requirement-layer parent; adopting the VO under REQ-ADAPTER-BOUNDARY is the minimal option, a new REQ the honest one.
details.mechanism: §5.5 step 1: the rust-cargo SourceDiscoveryAdapter enumerates `*.rs` beneath the adapter config `include` roots (詳細設計 §1.2 config sample L127/L161: `include: ["src","tests","crates"]`) through a `.gitignore`-compliant walk, with `target/` excluded, and hands the result to §5.1 `DiscoveryBatch` construction. Core (`vtest-scan`) never enumerates files, so the discovered population D that feeds test_traceability, Source Target indexing and diagnostics is exactly this walk's output.
details.existing_vo_check: Absent from the frozen 154. VO-REGISTRY-01/02 and VO-AGG-07 quantify over "every discovered test" but never fix what discovery covers; VO-EXIST-08 governs incomplete discovery, not scope; VO-REGISTRY-05, VO-ADAPTER-05/09 and VO-EXIST-07 govern ownership/delegation of the walk, not which files it visits. Stretching any of these to mean "VCS-ignored files are outside D" would import a premise none of them states. The shadow mapping already records TEST-SCAN-010 as `proves_no_vo: true, candidates: []`, and dogfood-ontology-gate-findings.json contains no entry rejecting a discovery-scope VO — so it was never considered, not deliberately dropped.

proposed_vo.claim: Files excluded by the repository's VCS ignore rules lie outside the rust-cargo adapter's discovery scope: such a file is absent from the DiscoveryBatch built from the configured include roots.

details.gate_check: A (REQ restatement): passes — no REQ states it. B (mechanism description): passes — truth-condition on discovery output, not on how the walk is built. C (undecidable): passes — membership in the batch is observable. D (compound): passes — one exclusion condition; `target/` exclusion is deliberately left out as a sibling obligation rather than and-joined. E (implementation-present-tense promotion): passes — grounded in §5.5, and the crate name is removed. F (test-presupposing): passes. G: rust-cargo specificity is permitted since the design normatively requires it. Residual weakness: the source is a pseudo-code block, weaker register than prose obligations.
details.rationale: The suspicion splits in three. (a) Adapter owns the walk — normative but already covered. (b) `.gitignore`-compliant scope — stated in the normative 本冊 §5.5 in the same する-register as step 2, whose E-SCAN-001 clause is indisputably binding (mirrored in the diagnostics table L838, covered by VO-EXIST-08); 「target/は除外」 uses the same 除外 verb the spec uses contractually at L483. That grounds YES. (c) "ignored files yield no E-SCAN-001" is stated nowhere — it follows only from step1→step2 ordering, so it is dropped from the claim and must not be read into it. Verdict YES, narrowed to (b).
